outcome: Preeclampsia or eclampsia superimposed on pre-existing hypertension
cohort: The study included 14,882 women with a diagnosis of polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) who had deliveries between 2004 and 2014, identified from a nationwide inpatient sample database.
finding: Women with PCOS and pregestational diabetes were significantly more likely to experience adverse pregnancy complications, including hypertension, preeclampsia, placenta previa, preterm delivery, and cesarean section.
mod_finding: Women with PCOS and pregestational diabetes were at an increased risk of delivery by cesarean section.
